rejected_findings.reason: Same as above — tick 0 never steps in either caller.

blockers.title: NOC queue rows: right-aligned util% glyph-collides the Best-effort lane's queue-count digit on every util ≥ 10% row
blockers.evidence: lane 2 count drawn left-anchored at bx+96 = px+364 (bx = px+52+2*108); util% right-aligned at util_r = px+NOC_PANEL_W-6-96 = px+402 (NOC_PANEL_W=504). IBM Plex Mono advance = 600/1000 em (all glyphs, measured from assets/fonts/ibm_plex_mono_regular.ttf). Raylib MeasureTextEx/DrawTextEx widths at size 18: '100%' = 46.2px -> ink span [355.8,402]; '99%'/'70%'/'16%' = 34.4px -> first-ink starts 368.6-368.8. Count digit '6' ink at 18px = [365.2, 373.6]. Ink intersection: '99%'-class first glyph overlaps digit ink [368.8,373.6] = 4.8px; '100%''s second glyph '0' ink [368.6,373.6] = 5.0px on the digit.
blockers.detail: Every queue row with util ≥ 10% (the normal busy case, incl. the 100% saturation showcase) draws the first util glyph on top of the Best-effort queue count. Mechanically proven from the shipped TTF + raylib advance semantics; contradicts the KYLE legibility PASS (flagged as a mechanical contradiction per the vision caveat).
blockers.recommended_fix: Re-anchor the right block: reserve ≥130px (util_r = px+NOC_PANEL_W-6-130) and/or narrow the lane pitch (108) or bar width so the lane-3 count's right edge (< px+376) clears the util% left edge with margin; re-capture the rail.

warnings.title: Tier line rates ship as 67/100/267 Mbps, not the briefing's 10/100/1000 Mbps ladder
warnings.evidence: Briefing unit model: 'narrow = 10 Mbps ... standard = 100 Mbps ... wide = 1 Gbps'. Shipped: SIM_TIME_SCALE 3333 pinned by standard=100 Mbps + 8-tick transit; rate = frame_bits x hz x S / transit gives narrow 66.66 / wide 266.64 Mbps.
warnings.detail: Independently verified deviation AND independently verified impossibility: a single SIM_TIME_SCALE forces rate ∝ 1/transit (10:15:40 u/s -> transits 12:8:3), so 10/100/1000 would need S = 500/3333/12500 simultaneously — a 6.7x-3x pace change, forbidden by the hard rules (byte-identical goldens, verified 48/48 green this round). Documented in the PR body. Needs the user's conscious blessing of the derived ladder.
warnings.recommended_fix: None in code (the hard rules force it). Surface to the user at merge; if the nominal ladder is wanted it is its own transit-rebalance + re-bless job.

warnings.title: tx-ring window semantics (expiry boundary, slot reuse at W, rebuild reset, defensive bounds) have zero direct tests
warnings.evidence: grep bundle_tx_record|bundle_tx_window across core/*test* and app/ -> no hits. Coverage is indirect: units_test pins the formula, stats_test pins two measured windows (util 4 / tx 962 at tick 12; util 0 / tx 750 at tick 3), the 48-demo harness runs stats-check live==replay.
warnings.detail: The honest counter's ring machinery — tick-keyed staleness, exact-window edges, rebuild zeroing, the defensive bounds — has no direct unit pins. Re-classified P0->P1 by verification (happy paths are pinned end-to-end); the advisory gate is CONCERNS, not FAIL.
warnings.recommended_fix: Add bundles_test cases: record at consecutive ticks, window read at exactly tick+W (expiry), same-slot reuse after W, rebuild reset with a populated ring, served==0 skip.

warnings.title: noc_pipe_rows predicate swap (carried>=cap -> util_pct>=red_pct) has no discriminating test
warnings.evidence: noc_overlay_test.odin:267-289 counts sections with an EMPTY pipes array — the row-count pin cannot distinguish the new predicate from the old or from an inverted one.
warnings.detail: The PIPES-section membership predicate changed semantics this PR; the measure/draw twins agree with each other (verified) but nothing pins the predicate itself. Display-only surface (no golden coverage — the NOC panel is not in goldens).
warnings.recommended_fix: Extend the row-count test: hand-built pipes with util_pct 89/90 and cap_units 0 to pin the >=red and cap-0 exclusion.

warnings.title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS (re-triaged from lens FAIL)
warnings.evidence: Lens classified the ring gap P0 -> FAIL. Verified coverage facts: P0 happy paths pinned (units_test formula + stats_test measured integration + 48-demo stats-check determinism); unpinned: ring boundary semantics (W2) + predicate swap (W3).
warnings.detail: P0 100% (verified), P1 gaps in the 80-89% band -> CONCERNS per the gate thresholds after verification re-triage.
warnings.recommended_fix: Close W2 + W3 to lift the gate to PASS.

notes.title: Zero-capacity link maps to ~800 Mbps (transit_ticks pb,0 -> 1), not 0; old cap>0 guard dropped from the display predicate
notes.evidence: transit_ticks returns 1 for capacity 0 -> line_rate_bps = 799,920,000. noc_pipe_rows dropped the cap_units>0 check (relies on util_pct=0 < red).
notes.detail: Unreachable with the shipped catalog (decay floor: narrow 10 x 500 permille = 5; PIPES/queue predicates exclude util-0 cap-0 rows). Defensive semantics are inverted for a degenerate case a future era (permille < 100) could create.
notes.recommended_fix: Return 0 from line_rate_bps when capacity == 0 (or guard the display call sites).

notes.title: Stale '96 px chip' comments contradict TRAY_CHIP_W 96->112 from the same diff
notes.evidence: main.odin: 'Compact form fits the 96 px chip'; units.odin: 'the 96 px chip budget'; tray.odin (same PR): '96 -> 112 so the link chips seat their network-native label'.

notes.title: node_health comment + PR body quote 'util 150%...' but the format string drops the 'util' prefix
notes.evidence: Comment: '"util 150% (load 1.5 KiB / 33 Mbps)"'; code: fmt.tprintf("%d%% (load %s / %s)", ...) — no prefix.
notes.detail: Doc/quote drift only; dropping the prefix is arguably an improvement (the node pct is a load metric, not link util — see N10).
notes.recommended_fix: Align the comment (and PR-body quote) with the shipped format.

notes.title: NOC section headers + noc_panel_rows default hardcode 90/6/512 while the predicates read catalog tunables
notes.evidence: Headers: 'PIPES AT/OVER 90% (HONEST)', 'QUEUE DEPTH VS E9 BOUND (6 PKT)', 'POOL VS E22 CAP (512 PKT)'; predicates read cat.balance.warnings.pipe_red_pct / lane_queue_packets / pool_max_packets.
notes.detail: Three-way agreement. Labels go stale if the catalog is tuned (e.g. red 85 keeps saying 90%). Pre-existing pattern, but this diff extends it to the threshold value itself (the old '100%' was a mathematical constant, the new '90' is the tunable).
notes.recommended_fix: Format the headers from the catalog values (tprintf with red_pct/bound/cap).

notes.title: Stats stream P-row grows an 18th field but the header marker stays 'v1'
notes.evidence: '# pp stats stream v1 - deterministic per-tick stats' unchanged; P header line gains ',<tx_octets>' + a semantics note.
notes.detail: Only consumer is the harness byte-compare (live==replay — both sides same format, verified unaffected). The marker is a comment, not a parser contract, but a future external diffing tool could be misled.
notes.recommended_fix: Bump the marker to v2 (comment-only) at the next stream change, or note the column addition in the header text itself (partially done).

notes.title: CSV literal test pins util=100 alongside tx_octets=0 — an impossible pair under honest semantics
notes.detail: The test pins the WRITER's column order (its purpose), but the fixture documents a pairing the derivation can never produce.
notes.recommended_fix: Set the fixture's tx_octets to 45000 (or util to a consistent value) so the literal doubles as documentation.

notes.title: Sub-Kbps/bps formatter tiers untested; compact form emits a unitless number
notes.evidence: units_test pins Kbps/Mbps/Gbps/KiB/MiB/B tiers + compact M/K/G; no pin for the bps tier or sub-1K compact; compact returns '100M' with no unit.
notes.detail: Cosmetic; the reachable rate values (66.6M-800M) never hit the unpinned tiers. Compact unitlessness is intentional (chip budget) and network-conventional.

notes.title: line_rate_bytes_per_tick has no production caller and its comment overstates it as 'the honest utilization reference'
notes.evidence: grep across *.odin (excl. tests): only the definition. util_pct_window divides by (window x cap_units) directly, never by bytes/tick.
notes.detail: Three-way agreement. Test-only export; the honest-util formula does not use it. Either wire it in as the reference the comment claims or demote the comment.
notes.recommended_fix: Delete it, or reword the comment to 'the game-scale view of the rate (display reference)'.

notes.title: Same-tick re-step accumulates each execution's served units into one slot (over-reporting tx for that tick)
notes.evidence: bundle_tx_record does tx_served[s] += served for a repeated tick key; step.odin: 'Same-tick re-steps are deliberately allowed ... the app never re-steps — documented, accepted.'
notes.detail: The events buffer has the same documented re-step caveat; the tx ring joins that class. Production never re-steps (app + harness); tests that re-step would see inflated tx/window stats.
notes.recommended_fix: One comment line in bundle_tx_record noting the same-tick re-step accumulation joins the documented step-contract caveat.

notes.title: Node health card pct remains backlog / throughput (node-load metric), not octet-counter utilization
notes.evidence: pct = units*100/throughput (unbounded — 150%); load + rate converted native this PR; the 'util' label prefix was dropped (N3).
notes.detail: Different quantity from the LINK utilization the NOC bug concerned: node-side un-forwardable load vs forwarding ceiling (pre-existing measure, tests pin it). Converting it to windowed served-work would change node-health semantics (sim state — goldens), out of the job's isomorphism scope. The label no longer says 'util', reducing conflation.
notes.recommended_fix: None required; if desired, a future job could window the node measure the same way.

notes.title: Sim pipe warnings stay queue-pressure-keyed while NOC rail tint rides honest util
notes.evidence: pipe_congestion = congestion_level(press[bs] x 100 / lane_bound_units) — queue pressure vs E9 lane bound; unchanged by this PR (not in diff).
notes.detail: Re-keying sim warnings to utilization would change serialized warning state/events -> golden movement (hard-rule violation). Queue pressure is the queue's OWN telegraph signal; the NOC rail's amber/red (70/90) verified to ride honest util_pct (noc_util_level). Defensible reading of 'warnings ride the honest metric' as the display surfaces.
notes.recommended_fix: None; document the split (rail tint = util, sim warning = queue telegraph) if the ambiguity resurfaces.

notes.title: Bundles struct doc still claims 'never serialized (pure function of the Topology)' but the tx ring adds rolling flow history
notes.evidence: Struct comment: 'Rebuilt on every topology change (rule 1); never serialized (pure function of the Topology)'; the new ring field comment (same PR) says 'DERIVED state ... Reset on every rebuild' — flow-sourced, not topology-sourced.
notes.detail: Field-level doc is right; struct-level doc is now false as written. Also units.odin:56-58 points at 'balance.json's era' where the documented health-window seam lives in the health section.
notes.recommended_fix: Update the struct comment: 'derived view — topology rows + replay-rebuildable flow-history ring; never serialized'.
